name: Spider nest identity
summary: On four qubits, the product of π/4 phase gadgets on all non-empty subsets of qubits, with sign (−1)^(k+1) for gadgets of size k, is the identity.
description:
A *spider nest* is a collection of [phase gadgets](../phase-gadget-fusion/) that multiplies to the identity. On four qubits, taking a gadget with phase $\frac\pi4$ on every qubit, $-\frac\pi4$ on every pair, $\frac\pi4$ on every triple and $-\frac\pi4$ on all four gives the identity. This follows from the identity $\sum_{\emptyset\neq S\subseteq[n]} (-1)^{|S|+1}\,\bigoplus_{i\in S}x_i = 2^{n-1}x_1\cdots x_n$ for bit strings $x$, so that for $n=4$ the total phase is a multiple of $2\pi$.

Munson, Coecke and Wang derived the spider nest identities for all $n$ from a decomposition of phase gadgets into AND gates: an $n$-qubit $\frac\pi4$-gadget equals a product of 1-gadgets with phase $\frac{(n-2)(n-3)\pi}8$, 2-gadgets with phase $\frac{(3-n)\pi}4$ and 3-gadgets with phase $\frac\pi4$, and moving the $n$-gadget to the other side gives the nest. Spider nests are used by de Beaudrap, Bian and Wang to reduce the T-count of circuits: whenever a circuit contains more than half of a nest, it can be replaced by the inverse of the other half.
parameter_notes: Shown for n = 4 qubits, where the gadget phases are ±π/4. For other n the 1- and 2-gadget phases depend on n, and the n-gadget has phase −π/4.

source.location: Section 5, spider nest identities (following the corollary on decomposing π/4 phase gadgets)
